item.title: Incarico di ricerca: The Critical Reception of Polish Literature in Italy, 1861–1939 (ROMA "La Sapienza")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-19 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Roma
Field: Classics, philology, literature, art history / 10/SLAV-01 Slavistica

This research aims to reconstruct the critical reception of Polish literature in Italy from the Unification to the outbreak of the Second World War, with a focus on the periodical press. The study will identify and analyze various forms of critical reception—such as reviews, biographical pieces, promotional articles, and commentaries—within Italian literary and cultural journals, examining how Polish authors were presented and evaluated. It will also consider the extent to which this reception may have relied on foreign critical sources. Field: Classics, philology, literature, art history / 10/FLMR-01 Filologie e letterature medio-latina e romanze

item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-23 12:00
Institution: Univ. PAVIA, Pavia
Field: Classics, philology, literature, art history / 10/HELL-01 Lingua e letteratura greca

This research programme, part of the broader project “School Culture” promoted by the Centre for Teacher Education at the University of Pavia, draws on the publication of the draft of the new NationalCurriculum Guidelines for upper-secondary schools and the intense debate that followed. It aims to contextualise Italian education policies regarding the teaching of Greek language and culture from the post-war period to the present day within the broader context of the cultural and symbolic meanings attributed to Greek ‘classicism’ at different times in contemporary European history. Field: Classics, philology, literature, art history / 10/ANGL-01 Anglistica e angloamericanistica

The person hired for this research position will collaborate on the core activities of the MuBi project, contributing to the collection, organization, and analysis of linguistic data regarding culinary microlanguage in multicultural contexts. They will participate in conducting ethnographic interviews in home kitchens, restaurants, markets, and reception centers, handling the preparation of protocols, contact management, and the collection of informed consent. item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Urban Memory and Active Citizenship: a model for the enhancement of Palermo's post-war sites through scientific comparison with the Chongqing case study (Univ. PALERMO)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-10-30 12:00
Institution: Univ. PALERMO, Palermo
Field: Classics, philology, literature, art history / 10/ASIA-01 Culture e lingue dell'asia centrale, meridionale, orientale e sud-orientale

This research proposal stems from a critical observation conducted in the urban context of Palermo: the presence of numerous ruins and sites marked by the 1943 bombings is today perceived in a distorted way by the local community and by visitors. During an observation experience at the University Language Centre (CLA), it emerged that even long-term foreign residents interpret the architectural "wounds" of the historic center as signs of mere building neglect, ignoring their wartime origin. This phenomenon of historical amnesia also profoundly affects the new generations of citizens of Palermo, for whom the disconnection between physical space and the memory of the events that shaped it is…

item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Narrating Natural-Cultural Heritage: Towards a Literary Mapping of the Global South, Starting from Sicily (Univ. PALERMO)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-10-30 12:00
Institution: Univ. PALERMO, Palermo
Field: Classics, philology, literature, art history / 10/COMP-01 Comparatistica e teoria della letteratura

This research project focuses on the apparent opacity of landscapes in relation to narrative. This resistance seems to be due, on the one hand, to the lack of attention that human history has always paid to the environment, and on the other, to the gaps in the available narrative forms, which are mostly oriented towards the human scale and the immediatepresent. Consequently, these have not been sufficient to capture the complexity of places where geological, ecological and historical time are layered without ever resulting in a linear narrative
